issues.problem: Tile lists come from gsplat (radius 3.33 sigma, eps2d 0.3, alpha cap 0.999, stop at next_T <= 1e-4) while the official uses 3 sigma radius, alpha cap 0.99 and stop at < 1e-4. The set of Gaussians per tile, and so the survivor count, differs slightly. Already documented as gap 2.
issues.fix: None needed. Compare compression ratio and delta PSNR, not absolute counts.

issues.problem: The prune runs after the optimizer step of step 20000. Official prunes before that step's optimizer.step (train.py:130 then :134), so the official survivors take one more Adam update at step 20000 on gradients computed before the prune. Negligible.

Official partial last batches write overflow slots into the next tile's range (a race, with an out-of-bounds write for the last tile) and unwritten slots (key -1, value 0) mark Gaussian 0. The port uses tile-private padded slots, so the entries survive deterministically and Gaussian 0 is not force-kept. Documented gap 1. The port's behaviour is a deterministic superset of the official.
issues.evidence: official slot = range.x + progress, progress = i*256 + thread_rank, written even when thread_rank >= toDo

issues.problem: The GT is cached as uint8 from the views the training loop happens to sample (20000 draws over ~150-300 views, so a miss is negligible and raises an error). This is lossless only if the dataset images are 8-bit, which holds for resized JPEG/PNG.

verified_claims: Official renderCUDA_topk_color: slot index = range.x + i*256 + thread_rank, overwritten by every contributing Gaussian of the batch (value collected_id[j]), so each pixel puts forward only the LAST contributor of each 256-Gaussian batch. Keys (tile<<32)|floor((1-score)*65535); the stable cub radix sort over the low 32+bit bits and markingTopKMasks keep the first k entries of each tile. So selection is top-k per 16x16 tile of per-pixel-per-batch samples, not per pixel. The port's selection='tile' reproduces this (same slot order, last-contributor overwrite, T before update, no write on the terminating Gaussian, same quantisation and stable tie-break) apart from the documented race.

Colour: prim_color = features = geomState.rgb, SH-evaluated per view at the active degree (3 at 20k), +0.5 and clamped >= 0. The port uses gsplat spherical_harmonics at runtime_sh_degree(20000)=3 with the camera position from the viewmat, and the training-resolution GT in [0,1]. Matches.

Prune schedule: code defaults are iteration 15000 and top-10, but benchmark.yaml (the paper sweep) sets [20000] and top-1 with score 0x24. The port defaults match the sweep and the paper. Union over scene.getTrainCameras() (the --eval train split). The port uses the train split.

Optimizer-state alignment via gsplat ops.remove on params, optimizers and strategy state is checked by the probe. Densification stops at 15000, so nothing else is altered; the rest equals the SplatStudio vanilla 3DGS baseline.

paper_results.json matches the arXiv Table 1/3/4/5 and WACV Table 3 values checked (mip360 27.073/0.7881/0.2688/350.3/88.9; baseline 27.434/0.8120/0.2219/3159.0; T&T 23.060/23.634/162.2/1829.2; DB 29.420/29.438/305.0/2804.7; NeRF 32.876/33.806; top-k sweep rows). All consistent.
summary: No critical or major issues. Verified against the official CUDA: renderCUDA_topk_color does keep top-k per 16x16 tile (last contributor of each 256-batch per pixel), and selection='tile' reproduces it exactly apart from the documented cross-tile race and Gaussian-0 artefact. Score_SG_36, the SH-evaluated per-view colour, the 20k/top-1 benchmark.yaml schedule (code defaults 15k/top-10 are not used), the view union and optimizer alignment are correct. The official resolution rule is -1 -> width 1600 when the image is wider than 1600, so mipnerf360-1600 is the right protocol; the vanilla baseline must be re-run at that resolution and bench notes updated. paper_results.json matches the tables.
